claims.text: An ab initio framework will improve predictive understanding of lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
The improvement over existing analytical approaches will be at least 20%.
The relevant initial material is a bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal that may contain defects and impurities such as 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed framework integrates advanced ab initio techniques into a Bayesian multi-objective optimization workflow.
The proposed prediction is applicable from 200 K to 1200 K.
Defects and impurities are components of the atomic-scale complexity relevant to heat transport in this alloy.
The framework will capture complex interactions between lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
Capturing those interactions will permit more accurate separation of lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
Improved prediction of the separate transport contributions will enable the design of high-entropy alloys with desired thermal properties.
Existing analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity.
Below 200 K and above 1200 K, HfNbTaTiZr may deviate from the trends predicted by the framework.
The framework's improvement and applicability limits depend on its specific implementation and validation.
Validation should compare predicted lattice, electronic, and total thermal conductivities with measurements on HfNbTaTiZr samples having varied defect and impurity concentrations.
Deviation of predicted values from experimental measurements by more than 30% will falsify the hypothesis.
